scientific_question: When transferring frozen Wave-2 A3 (trained/calibrated strictly on 6 Holter/ambulatory source DBs) to acute short-duration ICU/OR bedside recordings (MGHDB) with zero parameter or threshold retuning, which benefits of A3 transfer across clinical domains, and at which pipeline stage (Stage 1 vs Stage 2) is sensitivity lost?

primary.operating_point: Locked source-calibrated T1 (identical R3_B20 source calibration rule; isolates the 5 Branch-F:N/S primitives)
primary.unit_of_analysis_primary: Tier1_Explicit (merging 7 explicit cross-referenced multi-record patients; subject-summed counts & hours)

key_secondary_end_to_end.operating_point: Locked source-calibrated T1 (end-to-end gain vs Wave-1 reference)

supporting_controls: Linear LogR (identical pairs at locked T1)
Matched-FA curves (S_min sweep AND pure m_N sweep under fixed B0_R1 Branch-F:V gate) for threshold-independent ranking
Subgroup diagnostics: Active-Anchor (K_end > 0) subjects, S2-F+ (s2_F > 0) subjects, Excluding mgh247+mgh046

denominator_and_diagnostic_rules_locked.primary_recall_denominator: ALL post-prefix F+ subjects (including F+ subjects with s2_F == 0, whose full-system recall is 0.0%).
denominator_and_diagnostic_rules_locked.conditional_stage2_recall: Reported separately across s2_F > 0 subjects and pooled TP / s2_F to isolate Stage-1 admission ceiling vs Stage-2 ranking.
mandatory_four_numbers_side_by_side: Stage-1->Stage-2 admitted F beats / total post-prefix F beats (plus K_end > 0 subject/record count)
denominator_and_diagnostic_rules_locked.non_collapse_interpretation_rule: Both Delta_MacroRec_Fpos and Delta_MeanFAPH_All with 95% paired subject bootstrap CIs are reported side-by-side. FAPH reduction achieved by collapsing F recall toward zero is NOT counted as a representation gain; if recall and FAPH move in opposing directions, the trade-off is reported explicitly without claiming dominance.
